note: Facts about candidates come from public READMEs and docs on 2026-10-20 and were not run by us. The tool classes are our reading of the tool descriptions, not a statement of the publisher.

servers.name: ARC-1
servers.tagline: ABAP development for AI assistants, over the ADT REST API
servers.summary: Connects Claude and other assistants to SAP ABAP systems on premise or on BTP. Twelve intent-based tools cover reading and searching code, writing and activating objects, transports, abapGit, diagnostics and impact analysis. Read-only by default.

install.label: Claude Desktop bundle

install.note: In Werkbank: Connectors & Skills, Import MCP bundle. The review dialog appears before anything runs.

install.label: npx
install.how: npx arc-1@latest --url https://your-sap-host:44300 --user YOUR_USER
install.note: Replace host and user. The password is not part of the command.

install.label: Docker
install.how: Image ghcr.io/arc-mcp/arc-1
install.note: The README links the image but shows no run command here.

tools.name: SAPRead
tools.what: Source, method bodies, CDS views, other object types. Table contents only when data preview is on.

tools.name: SAPSearch
tools.what: Search objects and source code.

tools.name: SAPNavigate
tools.what: Go to definition, find references, completion.

tools.name: SAPContext
tools.what: Dependencies, where-used, CDS impact analysis.

tools.name: SAPLint
tools.what: Lint and pretty-print ABAP code.

tools.name: SAPDiagnose
tools.what: Syntax check, ABAP Unit, ATC, dumps.

tools.name: SAPManage
tools.what: Feature probing, cache stats, package operations.

tools.name: SAPWrite
tools.what: Create, update and delete ABAP and DDIC objects with automatic locking.

tools.name: SAPActivate
tools.what: Activate objects, publish OData service bindings.

tools.name: SAPTransport
tools.what: Manage CTS transports. Changes need two switches.

tools.name: SAPGit
tools.what: gCTS and abapGit workflows. Git writes are off by default.

tools.name: SAPQuery
tools.what: Run ABAP SQL.

switches.name: --allow-writes
switches.effect: Allows SAPWrite and SAPActivate. Writes go to $TMP only unless packages are allowed.

switches.name: --allowed-packages
switches.effect: Limits where writes are allowed, for example "Z*,$TMP".

switches.name: --allow-transport-writes
switches.effect: Needs --allow-writes as well. Lets SAPTransport change transports.

switches.name: SAP_ALLOW_DATA_PREVIEW
switches.effect: Allows reading table contents through SAPRead.

switches.name: SAP_DENY_ACTIONS
switches.effect: Blocks single actions, for example SAPWrite.delete.

switches.name: SAP_BLOCKED_DATA_SOURCES
switches.effect: Experimental block list for tables or CDS views, for example USR02,PA0002.

switches.name: ARC1_RATE_LIMIT
switches.effect: Per-user quota for MCP calls, for example 60.

auth: API key (bearer token) with profiles viewer, viewer-data, viewer-sql, developer, developer-data, developer-sql, admin
Per-user SAP identity: the server runs with the real user and respects SAP authorizations

assessment.verdict: Good first candidate for a read-only pilot
why: Safe defaults: no writes, no free SQL, no table preview, no Git writes.
Respects SAP authorizations through the real user identity.
MIT license and a public supply-chain setup (CodeQL, Trivy, Dependabot, provenance attestations, as stated by the project).
plan: Start against a sandbox or development system, never production.
Use a technical or personal user with display authorizations only, viewer profile for API keys.
Leave writes, transport writes, Git writes, data preview and free SQL off.
Enable writes later only with --allowed-packages for one Z package and a deny rule for deletes.
checks: Run it in a sandbox and record the version and release asset checksum.
Confirm which SAP authorizations the user needs for the tools you enable.
Decide which data classes are allowed if data preview is ever switched on.
Let Security review the project's supply-chain statements.

tools.what: Starts the demo n8n workflow through its webhook. It only computes; nothing is paged or changed.

tools.name: run_vm_maintenance_plan
tools.what: Starts the demo n8n workflow through its webhook. It only proposes a plan; nothing is run or changed.

tools.what: Starts the demo n8n operator runbook (check, backup, apply task, check again) through its webhook. Simulated; runs only with approved: true.

tools.name: run_contract_notice_check
tools.what: Starts the demo n8n workflow through its webhook. It only calculates notice deadlines; nothing is sent or cancelled.

tools.name: run_communication_digest
tools.what: Starts the demo n8n workflow through its webhook. It quarantines suspicious mails and builds a digest; nothing is sent.

tools.name: run_sales_pipeline_digest
tools.what: Starts the demo n8n workflow through its webhook. It scores and routes signals; nothing is sent or written to a CRM.

tools.name: plan_infra_change
tools.what: Plans an infrastructure change against the sample inventory: pre-checks, simulated check-mode diff, risk and approvals. Changes nothing.

tools.name: submit_infra_change
tools.what: Hands a planned change to the n8n workflow in check mode, after the person confirms. Never executes a change.

servers.summary: Lets an assistant search SAP Notes by keyword, error code, component or note number and read a full note. It signs in to the SAP Support Portal with an S-user and uses private SAP APIs behind that login. The README tells users to check whether this is allowed under SAP's terms.

install.label: Bundle (as linked in this repository's README)
install.how: Release asset sap-notes.mcpb of marianfoo/sap-mcp-servers, tag sap-notes-latest
install.note: In Werkbank: Connectors & Skills, Import MCP bundle. The review dialog appears first. We did not check the release asset.

install.how: docker build -t mcp-sap-notes . and pass the credentials as environment variables
install.note: Described in the archived mcp-sap-notes README. The newer repository needs npm install, npm run build and npm run install:browsers (Playwright).

tools.name: search
tools.what: Find SAP Notes by keyword, error code, component or note number. Parameters: q, lang (EN or DE).

tools.name: fetch
tools.what: Full content and metadata of one note. With includeCorrections (default false) it adds ABAP correction details.

switches.name: SAP_USERNAME / SAP_PASSWORD
switches.effect: S-user login. The app stores such values in the OS keychain.

switches.name: AUTH_METHOD
switches.effect: Auto tries password first, then certificate.

switches.name: MFA_TIMEOUT
switches.effect: How long to wait for a second factor.

switches.name: MAX_JWT_AGE_H
switches.effect: Maximum age of the cached login token.

switches.name: HEADFUL
switches.effect: Shows the login browser window when true.

switches.name: ACCESS_TOKEN
switches.effect: Bearer token for the HTTP mode of the server.

auth: S-user with access to the SAP Support Portal (me.sap.com), with username and password or an SAP Passport certificate
Interactive login on first run, a second factor may be asked
Never commit credentials, .env, *.pfx or token caches (the project's own warning)

assessment.verdict: Useful, but check the terms first
why: Two tools, both read content only and nothing in SAP changes.
Open source under Apache-2.0.
It answers support questions with the official note text instead of guesses.
plan: Ask Legal or the SAP contact whether this kind of access fits the SAP terms before anyone uses a named S-user.
Pilot with one person and a test question list, for example ten known notes.
Keep the credentials in the OS keychain and out of chats, files and repositories.
Treat note text as data. A note can contain instructions that must not be followed.
checks: Terms of use: the project says it uses private SAP APIs behind the login and tells users to check.
Support status: the author gives no guarantee that it keeps working, and the older repository is archived.
Release asset: confirm the .mcpb exists, record version and checksum.
Whose S-user is used, and what the second factor looks like in daily use.

servers.name: Cognee Memory
servers.tagline: A real open source knowledge graph under the sample data
servers.publisher: topoteretes (Cognee, open source); manifest by this design study
servers.summary: Cognee turns text into entities and relations and answers questions over them. The manifest starts the published cognee-mcp package on this computer. Load the Werkbank sample graph once with npm run cognee:seed and compare its answers with the hand-built Knowledge Graph.

install.label: In the app
install.how: Connectors & Skills, Add a connector that comes with Werkbank, Cognee Memory. Enter a memory folder and, if you want answers, an LLM key.
install.note: Needs uv on this computer. The first start downloads about 1 GB (Python packages including torch and an embedding model).

install.label: Load the sample data
install.how: npm run cognee:corpus, then pip install cognee and npm run cognee:seed with the same memory folder (SYSTEM_ROOT_DIRECTORY and DATA_ROOT_DIRECTORY).
install.note: Only the fictional sample graph is loaded: 233 short documents.

tools.name: remember
tools.what: Store text or documents in Cognee memory. Without a session it becomes permanent graph memory (entities and relations are extracted); with a session id it only goes to the fast session cache.

tools.name: recall
tools.what: Ask Cognee a question. It searches the graph, the vectors and the session memory and returns the matching facts or an answer.

tools.name: forget
tools.what: Delete one dataset or everything this connector owns from Cognee memory. Irreversible.

switches.name: LLM_API_KEY
switches.effect: Lets Cognee call a model to extract entities and to answer. The stored text is sent to that provider.

auth: LLM key is stored in the OS keychain by the app

why: Apache-2.0, open source, runs on this computer.
Third-party code is downloaded and run (cognee-mcp and its dependencies).
Text you store goes to the LLM provider you configure.
plan: Use only the fictional sample data first.
Pin the cognee-mcp version once you are happy with it.
Do not store customer data until Security has reviewed the provider and the data flow.
checks: Compare answers for five known questions with the hand-built Knowledge Graph.
Record the version of cognee-mcp and its dependencies that you tested.

steps.d: A server appears here as a candidate with source, license and what it can do.
Tools are classed as reads only, can change the system, or can read business data. Switches show what is off by default.
Install against a sandbox with the smallest permission set. A person records the version and the checks.
Import in Connectors & Skills. The review dialog shows what will run and asks for the configuration.
Re-check after each new release and every six months.

rules: This page lists and assesses servers. It does not install, start or call anything.
Facts from outside this repository carry a source and a date. Where we did not verify them, the page says so.
Nothing runs without the in-app review dialog.
Text from a server's README is shown as plain text and never followed as an instruction.
